research_concepts: defensive suppression of opponent H2-H1 change
persistence of defensive effects across seasons
counter strategy best and avoid matchups
methodological_questions: Is a defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change reproducible across split halves or across seasons?
How many team-seasons are needed to detect a stable team-level trait with this noise level?
Do selection on extreme H2-H1 values or regression to the mean inflate apparent reliability?
Are adjustments for opponent quality, pace, and game state (score margin, garbage time) required?

historical_evidence.finding: Split-half reliability of connector teammate-path quality Q_p at player-season level, n=102 connectors: Pearson r=+0.215 (p=0.0297), Spearman rho=+0.242, Spearman-Brown about 0.355, ICC(player-season)=0.216 with 78.4% of variance within player. Recorded failure evidence: split-half r=0.215 / SB 0.355 is too low to treat the metric as a stable scoutable trait.

Inferred defensive scheme-change labels: within-game change 319/523 (61.0%), cross-game change 298/440 (67.7%), 103/104 units and 52/52 series show a change; transition matrices near-uniform. Recorded caveat: the inferred label cannot separate real defensive adjustment from offense executing differently; no validation recorded.

Play-type PPP across playoff series game buckets (1197 pooled records, no CIs): DRIVE 0.889 to 0.949 (+0.060), CUT +0.114, PNR +0.087, PULL_UP -0.077, POST_UP -0.032. Recorded as 'NO CLEAR SIGNAL'; observational with selection caveats.
LLM counter selection vs deterministic BEST tier on 3 suppression triggers: agreed with BEST 1/3, picked AVOID 2/3; recorded caveat that 230+ disagreements would be needed.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Treating a player-season split-half derived trait (connector Q_p) as a stable, reliable attribute.
failed_approaches.why: Low measurement reliability (r=0.215, Spearman-Brown about 0.355, ICC 0.216); most variance is within-player half-to-half. Recorded as limited by LIM:low_measurement_reliability and RISK:MEASURE_RELIABILITY.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using inferred defensive-scheme labels to measure defensive adjustment.
failed_approaches.why: Label cannot distinguish defensive adjustment from offensive variation; near-uniform transition matrices are consistent with label noise. Recorded as LIM:label_or_classification_error and RISK:LABEL_ERROR.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Detecting a within-series trend in play-type PPP across game buckets.
failed_approaches.why: No clear signal, observational data, selection effects, and no confidence intervals. Recorded as E_unclear with LIM:selection_or_regression_to_the_mean.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Evaluating counter selection on suppression triggers.
failed_approaches.why: Only 3 triggers, far below the recorded requirement of about 230+ disagreements. Recorded as LIM:small_sample and RISK:SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER.

evidence_establishes: Split-half and player-level reliability metrics in this project's earlier work were low (FAM:SF-APPS-085), so a comparable reliability check on a defensive metric should be run before any claim of a 'reliable trait' is made.

Inferred labels and small or selected samples in earlier project work did not yield testable answers (FAM:SF-APPA-005, FAM:SF-APPS-010, FAM:SF-APPA-027), so the defensive H2-H1 metric must not rely on a derived label or on a small trigger set.
No retrieved record tests whether a defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is reproducible across halves or seasons.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether defensive effects on opponent H2-H1 change are reliable at team-season level. No retrieved record studies this metric or team-level defense.
What the reliability of this metric is, or what the expected split-half correlation is for team-level defense.
Whether the 120 team-seasons (30 teams across 4 seasons, as I infer from the data description) provide enough power.
Whether the playoff data (partial for 2025-26) can contribute usable units.
own_inferences: The 120 team-seasons likely correspond to 30 teams across the 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons. The playoff series are a much smaller subset and should be analysed separately or excluded.

With about 30 teams per season, a year-to-year correlation has a standard error of roughly 0.19 (about 1/sqrt(n) for n=30 per season pair). Only fairly large reliabilities (about r>0.4) would be detectable with confidence, which is a large effect for a noisy H2-H1 difference.
H2-H1 change in opponent scoring is sensitive to game state (blowouts, garbage time, fouling, pace changes), so it may reflect score margin more than defensive quality unless it is adjusted.

Selecting the most extreme defenses on one season's H2-H1 and then re-measuring them in the next season would inflate apparent persistence through regression to the mean. The reliability test must therefore use unselected, pre-specified splits.
Testing several H2-H1 definitions, windows, and adjustments would create a multiple-comparisons problem that must be controlled in advance.
uncertainties: The exact definition of H2-H1 (points per 100 possessions versus raw points, and whether it is opponent-scored or net) is not specified in the task or the retrieved records.
The records do not state how many defensive possessions or matchup minutes per team-season are available, which limits reliability.
The 2025-26 regular season is complete only from 2026-04-13, and its playoffs are partial before 2026-06-21, so the data version must be fixed before analysis.
No retrieved record covers team-level defense. SF-APPS-086 was mentioned as related in SF-APPS-085 but was not returned, so it is not cited and was not reviewed.

historical_effect.explanation: The historical evidence did not show that the question is already answered, but the earlier low-reliability result (SF-APPS-085) and the label and sample-size failures (SF-APPA-005, SF-APPA-027) changed the plan. The question is restated as a reliability test, which is the first thing the project should establish, not a claim that a trait exists. The design excludes derived or inferred labels, requires unselected pre-specified splits to control regression to the mean, and sets an explicit power threshold. Without that record, the study would more likely have proceeded directly to a trait claim.

blocking_constraints.text: Earlier split-half work in this project found low reliability (SF-APPS-085, r=0.215). A team-level H2-H1 defensive metric may be similarly noisy, so a 'reliable trait' claim may not be supportable.
About 30 teams per season and 120 team-seasons give limited power to detect moderate reliability. The test must state a minimum detectable reliability before data are seen.
H2-H1 opponent scoring is confounded with score margin, garbage time, pace, and opponent quality, which must be adjusted for.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests the reliability of a team's defensive effect on opponent H2-H1 change. The closest earlier work measured reliability for a different player-season metric (SF-APPS-085) and found it low. Label-based defensive work (SF-APPA-005), a play-type series trend (SF-APPS-010), and a counter-selection test with 3 triggers (SF-APPA-027) were all inconclusive or untestable. These records inform method risks but do not answer the question.

risks.text: H2-H1 opponent-scoring difference is a noisy difference of two noisy halves; split-half reliability may be low, as in SF-APPS-085.
With 120 team-seasons, power to detect a moderate reliability is limited; the test needs a pre-stated minimum detectable reliability.
Choosing the most extreme defenses on one season's H2-H1 and checking persistence inflates apparent reliability via regression to the mean.
Score margin, garbage time, pace, and opponent quality can drive H2-H1 change independently of defense.
H2-H1 is derived from the same points outcome being explained, so defensive effects may be mechanically linked to scoring outcome definitions.
Multiple H2-H1 definitions, windows, and adjustments create false-positive risk unless pre-registered.
Rule changes, pace shifts, and roster turnover across 2022-23 to 2025-26 can break season-to-season persistence and must be checked.
Inferred defensive-scheme labels (SF-APPA-005) cannot be used as the defensive measure.
If true team-level defensive H2-H1 effects are small, most tests will return a null result that does not show the trait is absent.

design.estimand: Test-retest reliability of team-level defensive effect on opponent H2-H1 change: the correlation between the adjusted effect estimated from one pre-specified half of games and the same estimate from the other half, and between seasons, for each team.
design.sample: Regular seasons 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, and 2025-26 (complete from 2026-04-13) for 30 teams, about 120 team-seasons. Playoffs excluded from the primary test and analysed separately as descriptive only. The data version is fixed as of 2026-10-06.
design.power: Pre-register a minimum detectable reliability of about r=0.4 (80% power, two-sided alpha 0.05, n=30 per season pair), and report the observed confidence interval. If the upper bound of the 95% CI is below 0.2, conclude the trait is not reliable at this sample size.
design.controls: Adjust H2-H1 for score margin at half, pace (possessions), opponent offensive quality, home/away, and garbage-time filtering (pre-defined threshold). Use per-possession measures. Compare with a permutation baseline that keeps team and game structure.
design.falsification: A reliability near zero after adjustment, or reliability that disappears when margin and pace are controlled, falsifies the claim of a stable defensive trait. A positive correlation that appears only in selected top-decile teams is treated as regression to the mean, not reliability.
design.multiplicity: Pre-specify one primary H2-H1 definition, one adjustment set, and one reliability metric. Other definitions are secondary with Holm correction.
design.decision_rule: Claim a reliable team trait only if the pre-specified split-half and cross-season correlations are both above 0.4 with lower 95% CI above 0.2, after adjustment and falsification checks pass. Otherwise report the trait as unsupported at this sample size. Do not use inferred labels (SF-APPA-005) or small trigger sets (SF-APPA-027).
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23 through 2025-26 regular seasons as available on 2026-10-06; 2025-26 regular season complete from 2026-04-13. Playoffs are excluded from the primary analysis and used only as descriptive checks; 2025-26 playoffs are partial before 2026-06-21 and must not be used in the primary test.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 4 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-10-06, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
A defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 120 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.
